question: Could you find out the average percentage of the total lifetime sales (LTV) that occur in the first 7 and 30 days after a customer's initial purchase? Also, include the average total lifetime sales (LTV). Please exclude customers with zero lifetime sales. The 7- and 30-day periods should be based on the exact number of hours-minutes-seconds, not calendar days.
sql:
-- Final query
WITH customer_first_payment AS (
    SELECT customer_id, MIN(payment_date) as first_payment
    FROM payment
    GROUP BY customer_id
),
payment_with_flags AS (
    SELECT p.payment_id, p.customer_id, p.amount, p.payment_date,
           cfp.first_payment,
           EXTRACT(EPOCH FROM (p.payment_date - cfp.first_payment)) as seconds_since_first
    FROM payment p
    JOIN customer_first_payment cfp ON p.customer_id = cfp.customer_id
),
customer_early_sales AS (
    SELECT customer_id,
           SUM(amount) as total_ltv,
           SUM(CASE WHEN seconds_since_first <= 604800.0 THEN amount ELSE 0 END) as ltv_7days,
           SUM(CASE WHEN seconds_since_first <= 2592000.0 THEN amount ELSE 0 END) as ltv_30days
    FROM payment_with_flags
    GROUP BY customer_id
    HAVING SUM(amount) > 0
)
SELECT 
    AVG(CASE WHEN total_ltv > 0 THEN (ltv_7days * 100.0 / total_ltv) ELSE NULL END) as avg_pct_7days,
    AVG(CASE WHEN total_ltv > 0 THEN (ltv_30days * 100.0 / total_ltv) ELSE NULL END) as avg_pct_30days,
    AVG(total_ltv) as avg_ltv
FROM customer_early_sales
